body:
Remote test runs have a no-babysitting dispatch shape (coordinator decision, Termal::Fable2 mailbox 4daa5b87 #5028, 2026-11-08, after Greg's 'why Codex 6 is babysitting testrun? this is a big problem as it consumes the tokens'). Every remote FULL or focused job: the agent starts one background script that survives its turn (setsid/nohup on Linux, the Start-Process equivalent on Windows). The script runs the standard launcher once, hostless, with TERMAL_* removed for that child only. An EXIT trap using the inherited TERMAL_CLI sends END once to the integration owner with the run directory and exit code. The agent then ends its turn: no polling, sleep-loops, log tailing, status reads, progress posts or load sampling. The integration owner runs no watcher either: if a run goes quiet, it reads `summary RUN_DIRECTORY` once on an ordinary wake.
Why hostless is unknown. Correction from Fable2 #5056: the earlier reason cited here (w-5e2f3fba987a, registration refused from an independent clone) is wrong, since that item completed on 2026-11-06 with origin registration and durable host-qualified remote waits, observation-only and uncredited. The shape stays for now. Open check, not urgent: whether a registered remote run plus the remote wait gives the runner a real wake and still produces test-ref evidence; Engram::Fable saw termal_resume_after_test_runs return 404 'test run is not indexed' for remote runs, so test that rather than assume it.
